source_text: Ut igitur quod egimus colligatur, nec ego dictis tuis fraudem intuli, nec tu attulisti aliquid, quod vel dilutiore pietatis colore perfunderes, nedum Scripturis testibus approbares. Nec hoc quod tu putas, intellexit Apostolus; nec alia prorsus in paradiso fuit conditio commixtionis, quam qualis nunc in coniugiis agitur quae a se instituta Deus, tam ipsorum conditione sexuum et qualitate membrorum, quam frequentata benedictione perdocuit. Quibus absolutis claret, cunctos qui a te decipiuntur, ira esse quam misericordia digniores, quoniam in excusationem criminum suorum, quae mala voluntate committunt, te auctore infamant nativitatem, ne corrigant actionem.
pass_a_gloss: That therefore what we have driven may be gathered, neither did I bring fraud upon your sayings, nor did you bring anything which you could even pour over with a thinner color of piety, much less approve by Scriptures as witnesses. Nor did the Apostle understand this which you think; nor was there altogether in paradise another condition of mingling than such as is now driven in marriages which God, instituted by himself, taught thoroughly, as much by the condition of the sexes themselves and the quality of members, as by a repeated blessing. Which things having been absolved it is clear, that all who are deceived by you are worthier of wrath than of mercy, since in excuse of their own crimes, which they commit by an evil will, with you as author they defame nativity, lest they correct action.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: To gather up what we have established: I did not deal fraudulently with your words, and you produced nothing you could cover with even a faint appearance of piety, much less prove by scriptural testimony. The apostle did not mean what you think. Nor was the condition of sexual union in paradise different from what now occurs in marriages. God has made abundantly clear that he established marriage, both by the constitution of the sexes and the character of their bodily members, and by his repeated blessing (compare Genesis 1:27–28; Genesis 9:1). Once these points are settled, it is clear that all whom you deceive deserve anger more than mercy. At your prompting they defame birth to excuse the crimes they commit by an evil will, rather than amend their conduct.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's name for the doctrine he attacks: evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
